text.p: - Slovenians nominated President Milan Kucan as the country's political person of the year. U.S. President Bill Clinton was nominated as foreign person of the year.
- Government on Thursday adopted a draft budget for the first half of 1997, setting government spending at 326.4 billion tolars ($2.3 billion) and income at 327.6 billion tolars.

- Kucan said he will name his candidate for prime minister of the new government after talks with the Constitutional Court, the central bank, and State Council. The decision is expected before the New Year.

- Centre-left Liberal Democrats said on Thursday they expect President Kucan to nominate current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek for the new prime minister, because they emerged as the strongest single party at the November 10 general election.

- Slovenia's only nuclear plant Krsko produced 6.6 percent more electricity than planned. Although Krsko had financial problems there were no security problems in its operation, Stane Rozman, head executive of Krsko said.
- President of the parliament Janez Podobnik on Thursday met representatives of Slovenia's organisations abroad.
- Inhabitants of Ljubljana said the most serious problems of the capital were traffic, air pollution and crime, a public opinion survey showed.
- The postal system, founded two years ago, said its 1996 profit was about 10 million tolars ($70,400) on revenue of 17.8 billion tolars.
- Manager of tourist company Kompas Turizem Janez Pergar said his company will merge with Kompas Holidays in the new year.
